system_description.narrative_title: Global AI infrastructure race and its geopolitical spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: A global competition to build AI compute capacity — from advanced chips to massive data centres and software models — is driving concentrated investment, industrial partnerships and supply‑chain realignment, while provoking regulatory, legal and security frictions between states and firms. The system is open: capital, technology, talent, information and regulatory pressure flow across borders, producing reinforcing loops (AI demand → chip/tools investment → more AI capability) and balancing tensions (export controls, IP disputes, energy constraints, safety incidents) that shape short‑ and long‑term trajectories.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: the AI compute stack (chip design and fabrication, ASML tools, Nvidia/GPU ecosystem, chipmakers like TSMC/Samsung, AI model developers and labs), data centre construction and power infrastructure, venture and corporate capital flows into AI startups and tools (e.g., Mistral, CoreWeave, Google investment), cross‑border technology transfer and IP disputes (esp. US‑China), regulatory and safety incidents from AI labs, and resulting market and industrial responses.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic order (international strategic competition, global trade and investment regimes)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and currency volatility
Energy and power infrastructure (data centre power, grid and fuels)
International trade, export controls and industrial policy
National security, espionage and legal/regulatory systems

variables.name: Global AI compute capacity
variables.description: The aggregate available compute resources (GPU/TPU cycles, cluster throughput) that can be allocated to AI training and inference worldwide.

variables.name: Advanced semiconductor fabrication capacity
variables.description: The installed production capability for advanced process-node semiconductors (wafer starts, output of critical chips) available to AI hardware supply chains.

variables.name: Capital flows into AI infrastructure
variables.description: The rate and volume of investment (venture, corporate capex, loans) directed toward AI compute, data centers, tooling and related infrastructure.

variables.name: Supply‑chain concentration
variables.description: The degree to which critical inputs, suppliers and production stages for AI hardware and tools are concentrated among few nodes or regions.

variables.name: Cross‑border technology transfer rate
variables.description: The frequency and volume of technical knowledge, tooling, software and tacit engineering practices moving across national borders.

variables.name: Export control intensity
variables.description: The strictness and scope of trade restrictions, licensing regimes and export controls applied to AI‑relevant technologies and components.

variables.name: Geopolitical security tension
variables.description: The level of strategic rivalry, sanctions risk and political friction affecting cross‑border technology and investment relationships.

variables.name: AI safety and incident frequency
variables.description: The occurrence rate of safety, misuse, leak or major security incidents linked to AI models, deployments or development processes.

variables.name: Energy supply reliability for data centers
variables.description: The stability and availability of electrical power and grid capacity that can be committed to data centers and compute facilities.

variables.name: Renewable power share of infrastructure
variables.description: The proportion of energy consumed by AI infrastructure that is sourced from renewable or low‑carbon energy sources.

variables.name: AI skilled talent availability
variables.description: The size and accessibility of the qualified workforce (engineers, researchers, operators) able to design, build and run advanced AI systems.

variables.name: Chip and model R&D intensity
variables.description: The rate of resources (person‑years, budgets) devoted to research and development for semiconductor design, tooling and AI model advancement.

variables.name: Regulatory compliance costs for AI infrastructure
variables.description: The economic burden (time, money, operational constraints) borne to meet safety, privacy, export and environmental regulations for AI infrastructure.

variables.name: Cybersecurity risk level
variables.description: The assessed likelihood and expected severity of cyber intrusions, data exfiltration, or system compromise affecting AI infrastructure.

variables.name: Market demand for AI services
variables.description: The aggregate demand from enterprises, consumers and governments for AI capabilities, models, and AI‑powered products and services.

variables.name: Environmental externalities from infrastructure
variables.description: The local and systemic environmental impacts (land use change, heat, emissions, water use) generated by large‑scale AI infrastructure build‑out.

catalysts.title: Google $15bn Finland AI infrastructure build
catalysts.description: Google's announced $15bn investment and purchase of nuclear power in Finland to build data centers and supply power, accelerating capacity and capital flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Google to invest record $15 billion in AI infrastructure..." and "Google to invest $15 billion... buy nuclear power in Finland."

catalysts.description: Major fabs' commitments to ASML's newest chipmaking tools drive production of larger, advanced chips and support AI hardware scaling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "ASML to work with major chipmakers..." and "TSMC, Samsung commit to ASML’s newest chipmaking tools..."

catalysts.title: Pentagon $5bn AI infrastructure funding talks
catalysts.description: Pentagon negotiations on a $5bn loan to fund AI infrastructure could direct public capital into compute capacity and deepen strategic stakes.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Exclusive | Pentagon in Talks to Get Into AI Infrastructure Funding With a $5 Billion Loan."

catalysts.title: Surge in AI hacking, rogue agents and model incidents
catalysts.description: Recent disclosures of multiple model hacks, rogue-agent misuse, and withheld models indicate an ongoing uptick in AI safety and security incidents.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Anthropic discloses fourth AI hacking incident...", "OpenAI’s rogue agents used at least 10 more sites", "OpenAI hack of Hugging Face."

catalysts.title: U.S. lawmakers push new AI rules post-Anthropic warnings
catalysts.description: Lawmakers' calls for new AI regulation following Anthropic researchers' warnings may raise compliance burdens and export scrutiny.

catalysts.title: Mistral €3bn raise boosts European AI funding
catalysts.description: Mistral's record €3bn raise injects capital into European AI ecosystem, supporting startups, hiring and R&D capacity.

catalysts.title: DOJ probe into Nvidia-Groq licensing deal

catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Huawei heads to trial in US..." and "Huawei Faces U.S. Criminal Trial Weeks Before Trump-Xi Meeting."

catalysts.title: U.S. states rescind data center tax breaks
catalysts.description: States revisiting or ripping up data-center tax incentives will raise effective costs and slow some regional data‑centre builds.
